chapter_title_ka: წასლვა ავთანდილისა გულანშაროთ და ტარიელის შეყრა
chapter_title_en: Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
გამოვლნა ზღვანი ავთანდილ მგზავრითა რითმე ნავითა,
პირ-მხიარული აცორვებს მართ ოდენ მარტო თავითა;
მას შეყრა ტარიელისა უხარის მით ამბავითა,
და ხელ-განპყრობილი გულითა არს ღმრთისა საესავითა.
stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil has crossed the seas in a certain ship for travellers. He rides glad-hearted all alone. To meet Tariel with such tidings rejoices him. With hands uplifted, with his heart he hopes in God.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1327; Wardrop Stanza 1303): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. ვარდის ფურცლობის ნიშანი, დრო მათის პაემანისა,
ეტლის ცვალება მზისაგან, შეჯდომა სარატანისა,
და სულთქნა, რა ნახა ყვავილი მან, უნახავმან ხანისა.
stanzas.english_translation: Summer was come, from the earth came forth verdure, the token of the rose bursting into bloom, the time of their tryst, the change of course by the sun, the setting out of the cypress-formed. He sighed when he saw the flower long time unseen by him.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1328; Wardrop Stanza 1304): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.english_translation: The sky thundered and the cloud rained crystal dew; he kissed the rose with his rose-like lips; he said: "I gaze on you with tenderly-observant eye; I rejoice to have converse with you in her (T’hinat’hin's) stead."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1329; Wardrop Stanza 1305): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. ტარიელისკენ იარნა მან გზანი საწყინარენი,
უდაბურნი და უგზონი, უცხონი რამე არენი,
და სადაცა ნახის, დახოცის ლომ-ვეფხნი მოშამბნარენი.
stanzas.english_translation: When he thought on his friend, the bitter tears flowed; he travelled those weary ways towards Tariel, deserted and pathless, unknown regions; lion and panther of the reedy thickets he slew wherever he saw them.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1330; Wardrop Stanza 1306): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ქვაბნი გამოჩნდეს, იამა, იცნა, თქვა: “იგი კლდენია,
სადაა, ჩემი მოყვარე და ვისთვის ცრემლი მდენია;
ღირს ვარმცა, ვნახო პირის-პირ, უამბო რაცა მსმენია,
და არ მოსრულ იყოს, რაღა ვქმნა, ცუდ ჩემი განავლენია!”
stanzas.english_translation: The caves came in sight, he was glad, he recognized them. He said: "These be the rocks where my friend is, he for whom my tears have flowed. I am indeed worthy to see him face to face, to relate to him what I have heard. If he be not come, what shall I do? Vain will have been my travail.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1331; Wardrop Stanza 1307): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“თუ მოსრულა, უღონიოდ შინა ხანსა არ დაზმიდა,
მინდორს სადმე წავიდოდა, მხეცისაებრ ველთა ვლიდა;
სჯობს, თუ შამბ-შამბ წავიარო”, იგონებდა, იხედვიდა,
და ესე თქვა და მიუქცია, მინდორთაკე წამოვიდა.
stanzas.english_translation: "If he be come, doubtless he would not tarry within; he would go somewhere into the plain, like a wild beast he would roam in the fields; it is better for me to go round by the rushes." He bethought himself, he looked about; thus he spoke and turned, he went towards the plains.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1332; Wardrop Stanza 1308): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მიაცორვებს და იმღერის მხიარულითა გულითა,
მართ სახელდებით უყივის ხმითა მით სიხარულითა.
ცოტაი წავლო, გამოჩნდა მზე სინათლითა სრულითა:
და შამბისა პირსა ტარიელ დგას ხრმლითა მომახულითა.
stanzas.english_translation: He canters along and sings with merry heart; he shouts to him by name with cheerful voice. He went a little farther, there appeared the sun in full splendour, at the edge of the rushes stands Tariel with sharp sword.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1333; Wardrop Stanza 1309): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.english_translation: Tariel had slain a lion; its blood anointed his sword. He stood dismounted at the edge of the rushes; his horse was not with him. He heard Avt’handil's shout, he was astonished; he looked at him, recognized him, started, ran towards him, bounded.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1334; Wardrop Stanza 1310): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ხრმალი გასტყორცა ტარიელ, მიჰმართა მისსა ძმობილსა,
ყმა ცხენისაგან გარდიჭრა, ჰგვანდა ეტლისა სწრობილსა.
მათ ერთმანერთსა აკოცეს, ჰგვანან ყელ-გარდაჭდობილსა,
და ხმა შაქრის-ფერად გაუხდა ვარდსა, ხშირ-ხშირად პობილსა.
stanzas.english_translation: Tariel flung aside his sword and went towards his adopted brother. The knight alighted from his horse; it seemed to him that he had attained his goal (?). They kissed each other; their necks were as if riveted together. There was the sugary sound of the rose frequently opening.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1335; Wardrop Stanza 1311): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ტარიელ მოთქვა ტირილით სიტყვა ნატიფი, მჭევრები:
სისხლისა ღვარმან შეღება წითლად გიშრისა ტევრები,
ალვასა წყარო ცრემლისა მორწყავს, ნაკადი ბევრები,
და “რათგან შენ გნახე, რა მგამა, პატიჟი მჭირდეს მევ რები.”
stanzas.english_translation: Tariel, weeping, uttered polished, exquisite words--the tear of blood dyed the jetty thickets crimson, the fountain of tears, many streams, waters the aloe: "Since I have seen thee, what matters it to me if eight pains oppress me?"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1336; Wardrop Stanza 1312): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.english_translation: Tariel weeps and Avt’handil was speaking to him laughing, he smiles, he opens his coral (lips), the flash from his teeth quivers; he said: "I have learned tidings which will please thee; now the flower will be renewed, the rose hitherto fading."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1337; Wardrop Stanza 1313): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ტარიელ უთხრა: “ჰე, ძმაო, კმარის, დღეს რაცა მლხენია,
ყოველი ჩემი სალხინო მინახავს, ნახვა შენია;
სხვად ნუ ყოს ღმერთმან წამალი, არცა რა მოგისმენია:
და კაცმანმცა სოფელს ვით პოვა, რაც არა საქმე ზენია!”
stanzas.english_translation: Tariel said: "O brother, that which rejoices me to-day is enough, in seeing thee I have seen all my comfort, whatever other balm God gives; hast thou not heard: How can man find in the world that which is not of Heaven's doing!" (?)
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1338; Wardrop Stanza 1314): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რა ტარიელ არ შესჯერდა, ავთანდილცა არ დაწყნარდა,
მის ამბისა დაყოვნება ვეღარ გასძლო, აუჩქარდა,
გამოიღო რიდე მისი, ვინ ბაგეთა ვარდი ვარდა,
და რა ტარიელ ნახა, იცნა, გამოუღო, შემოვარდა.
stanzas.english_translation: When Tariel was not convinced, Avt’handil was ill at ease, he could no longer delay to tell the tale; he hastened, he drew forth the veil of her on whose lips the rose blooms; when Tariel saw, he recognized it, seized upon it, started.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1339; Wardrop Stanza 1315): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. პირსა დაიდვა, დაეცა, ვარდმან ფერითა მკრთალამან,
სულნი გაიქცნეს, მოდრიკა თავი გიშრისა ტალამან,
და მისნი ვერ გასძლნეს პატიჟნი ვერ კაენ, ვერცა სალამან.
stanzas.english_translation: He recognized the letter and the fringe of the veil and unfolded them, he pressed them to his face; he fell, a rose pale in hue, his spirits fled, the watchman of jet bowed his head. Neither Caen nor even Salaman could bear sorrows like his.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1340; Wardrop Stanza 1316): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil gazes at Tariel lying lifeless; he flew to him, he set about helping him, the sweetly-speaking; he could not be of avail to the consumed one, completely burned up with fire; her tokens had laid hold of his life.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1341; Wardrop Stanza 1317): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ავთანდილ დაჯდა ტირილად, ტირს ხმითა შვენიერითა,
ყორანსა გაჰგლეჯს ხშირ-ხშირად, აფრთხობს ბროლისა ჭერითა;
გახეთქა ლალი, გათლილი ანდამატისა კვერითა,
და მუნით წყარონი გამოჩნდეს, ძოწსა ვამსგავსე ფერითა.
stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil sat down to weep; he mourns with melodious voice, full oft he tears his raven locks, he rouses them by seizing them with his crystal (hand), he brake the ruby polished with a hammer of adamant, thence issue streams which I likened to coral in hue.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1342; Wardrop Stanza 1318): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.english_translation: He scratches his face; blood flows from his cheeks while gazing at (Tariel). "What I have done neither madman nor fool hath done. Why did I in my haste pour water on a fire difficult to quench! The heart struck hastily by exceeding joy cannot bear it.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1343; Wardrop Stanza 1319): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე მოვკალ ჩემი მოყვარე, რა მმართებს გაწბილებულსა?
თავსა ვაბრალობ საქმესა, არ დასმით გაგონებულსა!
ცრუ კაცი კარგად ვერა იქმს საქმესა გაძნელებულსა,
და თქმულა: სიწყნარე გმობილი სჯობს სიჩქარესა ქებულსა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "I have slain my friend! What befits me disgraced? I blame myself for a deed not thought out with heed. A stupid man cannot do well in a difficult matter. It is said: 'Chidden slowness is better than praised haste.'"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1344; Wardrop Stanza 1320): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
უცნობო ქმნილი ტარიელ ძეს მსგავსად ნატუსალისად,
ავთანდილ ადგა, გამოვლნა შამბნი საძებრად წყალისად,
მან პოვა სისხლი ლომისა, მოაქვს სავსებლად ალისად,
და მკერდსა დაასხა, გავეხდა ლაჟვარდი ფერად ლალისად.
stanzas.english_translation: Tariel lay unconscious, as if scorched, Avt’handil rose, he passed through the rushes in search of water; he found the lion's blood, he carries it to quench the flame, he sprinkled it on (Tariel's) breast; the lapis-lazuli became ruby-hued.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1345; Wardrop Stanza 1321): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil sprinkled the breast of that lion (Tariel) with the lion's blood. Tariel started up, the ranks of the race of India moved, he opened his eyes, he received power to sit up; blue seems the ray of the moon diminished in ray by the sun.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1346; Wardrop Stanza 1322): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ზამთარი ვარდთა გაახმობს, ფურცელნი ჩამოსცვივიან,
ზაფხულის მზისა სიახლე დასწვავს, გვალვასა სჩივიან,
მაგრა მაზედა ბულბულნი ტურფასა ხმასა ჰყივიან,
და სიცხე სწვავს, ყინვა დააზრობს, წყლულნი ორჯელვე სტკივიან.
stanzas.english_translation: Winter makes the roses fade, their leaves fall; the ardour of the summer sun burns them, they bemoan the drought, but upon them nightingales complain with lovely voice; heat consumes, frost freezes; the wounds hurt them in either case.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1347; Wardrop Stanza 1323): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
აგრევე გული კაცისა მოსაგვარებლად ძნელია,
ჭირსა და ლხინსა ორსავე ზედა, მართ ვითა ხელია,
მიწყივ წყლულდების, საწუთრო მისი აროდეს მრთელია.
და იგი მიენდოს სოფელსა ვინცა თავისი მტერია!
stanzas.english_translation: Even so is it hard to deal with the heart of man; it is mad alike both in grief and in joy; it is always wounded, its fate is never whole. He only can trust this world who is his own foe.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1348; Wardrop Stanza 1324): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.english_translation: Tariel gazed again on the writing of his slayer; he reads, though the reading of her letter maddens him; his tears blind him to the light, dark seems the beam of day. Avt’handil rose, he began to speak with rough? words.

იტყვის თუ: “ნაქმრად არ ვარგა კაცისა გასწავლილისად,
აწ რადღა გვმართებს ტირილი, ხამს დავსხდეთ ქმნად ღიმილისად,
ადეგ, წავიდეთ საძებრად მის მზისა წარხდომილისად!
და ადრე მიგიყვან, მიყვანა არს შენგან მონდომილი სად.
stanzas.english_translation: He said: "Such behaviour is unworthy of an instructed man! Why should we weep now? It behoves us to set about the making of smiles. Arise, let us go in quest of that lost sun. Soon shall I lead thee to her; I must bring thee to thy desired one.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1350; Wardrop Stanza 1326): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ვითა გვმართებს გახარება, პირველ აგრე გავიხარნეთ,
მერმე შევსხდეთ, გავემართნეთ, ქაჯეთისკენ თავნი ვარნეთ,
ხრმალნი ჩვენნი ვიწინამძღვრნეთ, მათნი ზურგით დავიყარნეთ,
და უჭირველნი შემოვიქცეთ, იგი მძორთა დავადარნეთ”.
stanzas.english_translation: "What joy befits us, therewithal let us first rejoice. Then let us mount and set out, let us wend towards Kadjet’hi. Be our swords our guides, let us sheath them in their (the Kadjis') backs; untroubled shall we return, we shall reduce them to carrion."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1351; Wardrop Stanza 1327): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მერმე ტარიელ ამბავსა ჰკითხავს, აღარა ბნდებოდა.
შეჰხედნის, თვალნი ამართნის, შავ-თეთრი ელვა კრთებოდა,
მართ ვითა ლალსა მზისაგან მას ფერი ეზარდებოდა;
და ვინ ღირსა, თუმცა წყალობით ცა მიწყივ მობრუნდებოდა!
stanzas.english_translation: Then Tariel asks for tidings; he no longer fainted. He looked up, he raised his eyes, the black and white lightning glittered, as a ruby by the sun so was his colour increased. Who is worthy that towards him the sky turn ever in mercy?
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1352; Wardrop Stanza 1328): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ავთანდილს მადლი უბრძანა, ქმნა უყო საუბარისა:
“მე შენი ქება ვითა ვთქვა, ბრძენთაგან საქებარისა!
ვითა ზემთისა წყარომან, მოჰრწყე ყვავილი ბარისა,
და დამწყვიდე დენა ცრემლისა, ნარგისთა ნაგუბარისა”.
stanzas.english_translation: To Avt’handil he gave thanks; he conversed with him: "How shall I speak thy praise, worthy to be praised by the wise! Like a spring up on a mountain thou hast watered the flower of the plain; thou hast cut off for me the flow of tears of the pool of the narcissi (the eyes).
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1353; Wardrop Stanza 1329): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე ვერა გიყო ნაცვალი, ღმერთი გარდგიხდის ციერი,
ზეგარდმო მისით შემოგზღოს მუქაფა ჩემმაგიერი!”
შესხდეს და შინა წავიდეს, მათ ლხინი ჰქონდა ძლიერი;
და აწ გავეაძღო სოფელმან ასმათ, ადრითგან მშიერი.
stanzas.english_translation: "I can never make thee a return; may the God of heaven repay thee! May He in my stead reward thee from His height!" They mounted and went home; they made great rejoicing. Now the world (Fate) will indeed sate Asmat’h so long hungering.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1354; Wardrop Stanza 1330): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ქვაბისა კარსა ასმათი მარტო ზის, არ-ბარგოსანი.
შეჰხედნა, იცნა ტარიელ, თანა ყმა ჭარმაგოსანი.
ორნივე ტურფად იმღერდეს, ვით იადონი მგოსანი,
და მაშინვე იცნა, ავარდა მოშლილი პერანგოსანი.
stanzas.english_translation: At the door of the cave Asmat’h sits alone, not fully dressed; when she had looked she recognized Tariel, and with him a knight on a white horse; both were sweetly singing like songster nightingales. Immediately she recognized them she rose hastily, bare but for her smock.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1355; Wardrop Stanza 1331): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
აქამდის მიწყივ ენახა ქვაბს მისლვა მოტირალისა,
აწ გაუკვირდა დანახვა სიცილით მომღერალისა.
ზარ-აღებული ავარდა, ცნობა უც, ვითა მთრვალისა,
და არ იცის სმენა ამბისა ჯერ მისგან სასურვალისა.
stanzas.english_translation: Hitherto she had ever seen him come to the cave weeping, now she wondered to behold him singing, laughing; seized with fear she arose, her understanding was like a drunkard's; she heard not yet the news she so longed for.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1356; Wardrop Stanza 1332): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.english_translation: When they saw her they shouted to her, laughing and showing their teeth: "Ho! Asmat’h! God's mercy is come down on us from on high; we have found the lost moon; what we desired that have we done; now we shall have our fires quenched by Fate, our sorrows turned to joy."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1357; Wardrop Stanza 1333): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ავთანდილ ცხენსა გარდახდა ასმათის მოსახვეველად.
მან მიჰყო ხელი ალვასა, შტო მოჰყვა მოსარხეველად,
ყელსა და პირსა აკოცებს, არის ცრემლისა მფრქვეველად;
და “რა ჰქმენო, რა სცან, მიამბე, ვტირ შენი მოაჯე ველად”.
stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil alighted from his horse to embrace Asmat’h; she laid hold of the aloe, pliant to the touch was its branch (his arm); she kisses his neck and face; she sheds tears. "Tell me what thou hast discovered, what thou hast done. Beseeching thee, I weep on the field."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1358; Wardrop Stanza 1334): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil gave to Asmat’h the letter of her charge, the aloe with faded branch, the pale moon. He said: "See the writing of her who hath passed through troubles; the sun approaches us, it hath given us the putting away of shadow."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1359; Wardrop Stanza 1335): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ასმათ რა ნახა უსტარი, ცნა მისი დანაწერობა,
გაკვირდა, ზარმან აიღო, ათრთოლებს, ვითა ხელობა,

stanzas.english_translation: When Asmat’h saw the letter she knew (Nestan's) hand; she marvelled, fear seized her, she quakes like one possessed, from head to foot overwhelming wonder laid hold on her; she says: "What have I seen, what do I heard is it indeed true?"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1360; Wardrop Stanza 1336): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ავთანდილ უთხრა: “ნუ გეშის, ეგე ამბავი მრთელია;
ლხინი მოგვეცა, მოგვშორდა ყოველი ჭირი ძნელია,
მზე მოგვეახლა, უკუნი ჩვენთვის აღარა ბნელია,
და ბოროტსა სძლია კეთილმან, — არსება მისი გრძელია!”
stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil said: "Fear not, this story is true, joy is given to us, all sore grief is put away from us, the sun is come nigh us, darkness is no longer dark for us. Good hath overcome ill; the essence of (good) is lasting."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1361; Wardrop Stanza 1337): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.english_translation: The King of the Indians merrily spoke somewhat with Asmat’h; they embraced each other, joy made them weep; the raven's tail (eyelashes) dropped light dew upon the rose (cheeks). God forsaketh not man if man comprehend this.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1362; Wardrop Stanza 1338): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ღმერთსა მისცეს დიდი მადლი, თქვეს: “ გვიყოო, რაცა სჯობდა;
აწყა ვცანით, უარესსა პირი თქვენი არ გაბრჭობდა”.
ინდოთ მეფე მხიარული ხელ-განპყრობით ამას ხმობდა.
და ქვაბს შევიდეს მხიარული, ასმათ რასმე მასპინძლობდა.
stanzas.english_translation: They gave God great thanks. They said: "Thou hast done to us what was best; now we recognize that your mouth would not have adjudged to us the worst." The King of the Indians, with uplifted hand, joyously shouted this. Merry they went into the caves; Asmat’h made ready somewhat for their refreshment.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1363; Wardrop Stanza 1339): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ტარიელ ეტყვის ავთანდილს: “ისმინე სიტყვა ასები,
გიამბობ რასმე ამბავსა, მოამბედ ნუ გენასები:
მე ოდეს ქვაბნი წაუხვენ, დავხოცე დევთა დასები,
და მას აქათ მათი აქა ძეს საჭურჭლე ძვირ-ნაფასები”.
stanzas.english_translation: Tariel said to Avt’handil: "Hearken to these words: I will tell thee something, think me not a tedious narrator. Since the time when I captured the caves (and) slew droves of Devis, their precious treasury lies here.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1364; Wardrop Stanza 1340): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მე აგრე არა მინახავს, მართ ვითა არა მნდომია;
მოდი და გავხსნათ, შევიგნეთ, საჭურჭლე თუ რა ზომია”.
ეამა, ადგეს ორნივე, არცა ქვე ასმათ მჯდომია,
და დალეწეს კარი ორმოცი, მათგან არ ზედა ომია.
stanzas.english_translation: "Never have I seen it, for I have not wished to do so. Come and let us open it; let us see how much treasure there is." It pleased him; both arose, nor did Asmat’h stay seated. They broke down forty doors; it was no great struggle for them.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1365; Wardrop Stanza 1341): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
პოვეს საჭურჭლე უსახო, კვლა უნახავი თვალისა,
მუნ იდვა რიყე თვალისა, ხელ-წმიდად განათალისა,
ჩნდის მარგალიტი ოდენი ბურთისა საბურთალისა;
და ვინმცა ქმნა რიცხვი ოქროსა, ვერვისგან დანათვალისა!?
stanzas.english_translation: They found unequalled treasure, hitherto unseen by their eyes. There stood a heap of jewels of fair workmanship. There were seen pearls each as big as a ball for play. Who could make account of the gold not to be numbered by any!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1366; Wardrop Stanza 1342): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. After reviving the overwhelmed Tariel, they open the sealed treasure-chambers of the cave and arm themselves with invulnerable Kadji-forged armor and swords.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
იგი სახლი ორმოცივე შიგან იყო გატენილი.
პოეს ერთი ზარადხანა, აბჯრისათვის სახლად ქმნილი;
მუნ აბჯარი ყოვლი-ფერი ასრე იდვა, ვითა მწნილი,
და შიგან ერთი კიდობანი დაბეჭდილი, არ-გახსნილი.
stanzas.english_translation: Inside those forty rooms were full. They found an armoury newly made for armour; there all kinds of armour were placed like preserves (in a store cupboard); therein was a coffer, sealed, unopened.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1367; Wardrop Stanza 1343): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.english_translation: Upon it was written: "Here lieth wondrous armour: chain helmet, habergeon, steel-cutting sword. If the Kadjis attack the Devis it will be a hard day. Whoever openeth at any other time is a slayer of kings!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1368; Wardrop Stanza 1344): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
კიდობანი გახსნეს, პოეს მუნ აბჯარი სამი ტანი,
რასაცა ვით შეიმოსენ მეომარნი სამნი ყმანი,
ჯაჭვი, ხრმალი, მუზარადი, საბარკული მათი გვანი,
და ზურმუხტისა ბუდებითა იყვნეს ვითა ლუსკუმანი.
stanzas.english_translation: They opened the coffer; they found in it three suits of armour fit for three warrior knights to don; coats of mail, swords, helmets, greaves of like sort; they were in emerald nests, as it were shrines.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 53 ('Departure of Avtandil from Gulansharo and his Meeting with Tariel', Stanza 1369; Wardrop Stanza 1345): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails from Gulansharo, rides joyously to the cave, finds Tariel standing by the reeds with a freshly slain lion, and presents Nestan-Darejan's letter and veil token. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
თვითომან თვითო ჩაიცვეს, თავის თავს გამოსცდიდიან,
ჯაჭვ-მუზარადსა, აბჯარსა მართ ვერა ვერ მოჰკიდიან;
ხმალი რკინისა მოჰკრიან, ვით ბამბის მკედსა სჭრიდიან,
და მათ უღირს ყოვლად ქვეყანად, შევატყევ, არ გაჰყიდიან.
stanzas.english_translation: Each clothed himself with each, they tested them on themselves; chain helmet and habergeon nought could dint; they struck the swords on iron, they cut it like cotton-thread. I tell you they prize them more than all the world; they would not barter them for it.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
თქვეს: “ესე ნიშნად გვეყოფის, ვართო კარგითა ბედითა;
ღმერთმან მოგვხედნა თვალითა, ზეგარდმო მონახედითა”.
აიღეს იგი აბჯარი თავის თავისა ქედითა,
და თვითო მათ, ერთი ფრიდონის საძღვნობლად შეკრეს ღვედითა.
stanzas.english_translation: They said: "As a sign this is enough for us; we are in good luck. God has gazed on us with His eye, looking down from above." They took up that armour, each put it on his neck; they bound up one (set) with leather thongs to present to P’hridon.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ოქროც რამე წაიტანეს, მარგალიტი ღარიბები;
გამოვიდეს, გამობეჭდეს ორმოცივე საჭურჭლები.
ავთანდილ თქვა: “ამას იქით დავმაგრო ხრმალთა ნები,
და ამას ღამე არსად წავალ, რა გათენდეს, არ დავდგები”.
stanzas.english_translation: They took with them some gold, some rare pearls; they went forth, they sealed up the forty treasuries. Avt’handil said: "Henceforth will I fasten my palm to the sword; nowhere shall I go to-night, when day dawns I shall not tarry."

იგი მიჯნურნი მნათობთა, სხვისა ვერვისგან სწრობილნი,

stanzas.english_translation: Now, painter, limn the sworn brothers more steadfast than brothers, these lovers of stars, excelled by none, both heroic knights renowned in bravery. When they go to Kadjet’hi you shall see a battle of piercing lances.
